chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Mansur ibn Yunus from Shu'ayb al-Haddad from Bashshar ibn Yasar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells goods for women (slaves), and then buys them back from the owner who sold them to him. He said, 'Yes, there is no objection to it.' I said to him, 'I buy my goods.' He said, 'It is not your goods, nor your cattle, nor your sheep.'

key_terms.بِالنِّسَاءِ: for women / with women (often referring to female slaves in this context)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no objection to it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods for slaves and buy them back from the seller?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of selling movable goods (*mata'*) in exchange for female slaves, a common commodity in early Islamic commerce, while clarifying that this specific barter structure differs from simply repurchasing one's own original property. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic focus on the precise nature of the exchanged assets and the contractual intent, ensuring the transaction is not merely a circular exchange of identical items but a valid sale of distinct commodities.
